source_text: Ἀλλ᾿ οἱ πονεῖν ἕτοιμοι ἐπὶ τοῖς καλλίστοις οὐ πρότερον ἀποστήσονται ζητοῦντες τὴν ἀλήθειαν πρὶν ἂν τὴν ἀπόδειξιν ἀπ᾿ αὐτῶν λάβωσι τῶν γραφῶν. ἔστι μὲν οὖν κοινά τινα τῶν ἀνθρώπων κριτήρια καθάπερ τὰ αἰσθητήρια. τὰ δ᾿ ἄλλα τῶν βουληθέντων καὶ ἀσκησάντων τὰ ἀληθῆ. τὰ διὰ νοῦ καὶ λογισμοῦ τεχνικὰ λόγων ἀληθῶν τε καὶ ψευδῶν. μέγιστον δὲ τὸ καὶ τὴν οἴησιν ἀποθέσθαι. ἐν μέσῳ καταστάντας ἀκριβοῦς ἐπιστήμης καὶ προπετοῦς δοξοσοφίας, καὶ γνῶναι ὅτι ὁ τὴν αἰώνιον ἐλπίζων ἀνάπαυσιν γιγνώσκει καὶ τὴν εἴσοδον αὐτῆς ἐπίπονον οὖσαν καὶ »τεθλιμμένην«. ὁ δὲ ἅπαξ εὐαγγελισθεὶς καὶ »τὸ σωτήριόν« φησιν »ἰδών«, ἐν ᾗ ὥρᾳ ἂν ἐπιγνῷ, μὴ »ἐπιστρεφέσθω εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω καθάπερ ἡ Αὼτ γυνὴ« μηδὲ εἰς τὸν πρότερον βίον τὸν τοῖς αἰσθητοῖς προσανέχοντα, μηδὲ μὴν εἰς τὰς αἱρέσεις παλινδρομείτω· ἐρίζουσι γὰρ ἁμῇ γέ πῃ, τὸν ὄντα μὴ γινώσκουσαι θεόν. »ὁ γὰρ φιλῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα ὑπὲρ ἐμέ«, τὸν ὄντως πατέρα καὶ διδάσκαλον τῆς ἀληθείας, τὸν ἀναγεννῶντα καὶ ἀνακτίζοντα καὶ τιθηνούμενον τὴν ψυχὴν τὴν ἐξειλεγμένην, »οὐκ ἔστι μου ἄξιος«, ἄξιος λέγει τοῦ εἶναι υἱὸς θεοῦ καὶ μαθητὴς θεοῦ ὁμοῦ καὶ φίλος καὶ συγγενής. »οὐδεὶς γὰρ εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω βλέπων καὶ ἐπιβάλλων τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ ἐπ᾿ ἄροτρον εὔθετος τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ.« Ἀλλ᾿. ὡς ἔοικεν. τοῖς πολλοῖς καὶ μέχρι νῦν δοκεῖ ἡ Μαριὰμ λεχὼ εἶναι διὰ τὴν τοῦ παιδίου γέννησιν, οὐκ οὖσα λεχώ (καὶ γὰρ μετὰ τὸ τεκεῖν αὐτὴν μαιωθεῖσάν φασί τινες παρθένον εὑρεθῆναι)· τοιαῦται δ᾿ ἡμῖν αἱ κυριακαὶ γραφαί, τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἀποτίκτουσαι καὶ μένουσαι παρθένοι μετὰ τῆς ἐπικρύψεως τῶν τῆς ἀληθείας μυστηρίων. »τέτοκεν καὶ οὐ τέτοκεν«, φησὶν ἡ γραφή, ὡς ἂν ἐξ αὑτῆς. οὐκ ἐκ συνδυασμοῦ συλλαβοῦσα. διόπερ τοῖς γνωστικοῖς κεκυήκασιν αἱ γραφαί, αἱ δὲ αἱρέσεις οὐκ ἐκμαθοῦσαι ὡς μὴ κεκυηκυίας παραπέμπονται. πάντων δὲ ἀνθρώπων τὴν αὐτὴν κρίσιν ἐχόντων οἱ μὲν ἀκολουθοῦντες τῷ αἱροῦντι λόγῳ ποιοῦνται τὰς πίστεις, οἱ δὲ ἡδοναῖς σφᾶς αὐτοὺς ἐκδεδωκότες βιάζονται πρὸς τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τὴν γραφήν. δεῖ δ᾿, οἶμαι, τῷ τῆς ἀληθείας ἐραστῇ ψυχικῆς εὐτονίας· σφάλλεσθαι γὰρ ἀνάγκη μέγιστα τοὺς μεγίστοις ἐγχειροῦντας πράγμασιν, ἢν μὴ τὸν κανόνα τῆς ἀληθείας παρ᾿ αὐτῆς λαβόντες ἔχωσι τῆς ἀληθείας. οἱ τοιοῦτοι δέ, ἅτε ἀποπεσόντες τῆς ὀρθῆς ὁδοῦ. κἀν τοῖς πλείστοις τῶν κατὰ μέρος σφάλλονται εἰκότως. διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ἀληθῶν καὶ ψευδῶν κριτήριον συγγεγυμνασμένον ἀκριβῶς τὰ δέοντα αἱρεῖσθαι. εἰ γὰρ ἐκέκτηντο, ταῖς θείαις ἐπείθοντο ἂν γραφαῖς.
pass_a_gloss: But those who are ready to labor for the best things will not stop seeking the truth until they receive proof from the scriptures. For there are certain common criteria of men, such as the senses. But for those who have willed and practiced the truth, there are technical words of truth and falsehood through the mind and reason. The greatest thing, however, is to lay aside opinion. Having stood in the middle of precise knowledge and hurried dogma, and knowing that the one who hopes for eternal rest also knows that its entrance is laborious and 'afflicted'. The one who has once been evangelized and says 'I have seen the salvation' - in whichever hour he recognizes - should not turn back to what is behind, like the woman Lot, nor to the former life that yields to the senses, nor should he waver into the heresies; for they contend in a similar way, not knowing the existing God. 'For the one who loves father or mother more than me' - the true Father and teacher of truth, who regenerates and renews and nourishes the chosen soul - 'is not worthy of me', says the one worthy of being son of God and disciple of God, friend and relative. 'For no one looking back and putting his hand on the plow is fit for the kingdom of God.' But, as it seems, to many even now Mary appears to be a woman in childbirth because of the birth of the child, though she is not a woman in childbirth (for some say that after giving birth, she was found to be a virgin); such are the Lord's scriptures to us, giving birth to the truth and remaining virgins after the covering of the mysteries of truth. 'She has borne and has not borne', the scripture says, as if from itself, not having conceived from a union. Therefore, the scriptures have been impregnated with the truth for the knowledgeable, but the heresies, not having learned as if they had not been impregnated, are sent away. All men having the same judgment, some follow the choosing word and make their beliefs, while others, having given themselves over to pleasures, force the scripture towards their desires. But, I think, the lover of truth needs psychic strength; for it is necessary for those attempting the greatest matters to fail greatly, unless they have taken the standard of truth from truth itself. Such people, having fallen away from the right path, reasonably fail in most things, because they do not have a criterion of true and false things, trained precisely to choose what is necessary. For if they had it, they would obey the divine scriptures.

pass_b_english: But those ready to labor for the best things will not cease seeking the truth until they receive proof from the Scriptures. (Matthew 10:37; Luke 9:62)

Certain criteria are common to all people, such as the senses. But for those who have willed and practiced the truth, there are technical words of truth and falsehood through the mind and reason. The greatest thing, however, is to lay aside one's own opinion.

Standing midway between precise knowledge and rash dogma, one comes to know that the person who hopes for eternal rest also knows that its entrance is laborious and "afflicted." The one who has once been evangelized and says, "I have seen the salvation" — in whatever hour he recognizes it — must not turn back to what lies behind, like Lot's wife, nor to the former life that yields to the senses, nor should he waver back into the heresies; for they contend in a similar way, not knowing the true God. (Luke 9:62; Matthew 10:37)

'For the one who loves father or mother more than me' — the true Father and teacher of truth, who regenerates, renews, and nourishes the chosen soul — 'is not worthy of me,' says the One worthy of being Son of God and disciple of God, friend and relative. 'For no one looking back and putting his hand to the plow is fit for the kingdom of God.' (Matthew 10:37; Luke 9:62)

But, as it seems, to many even now Mary appears to be a woman in childbirth because of the child's birth, though she is not a woman in childbirth (for some say that after giving birth she was found to be a virgin). Such are the Lord's Scriptures to us: they give birth to the truth and remain virgins after the covering of the mysteries of truth. "She has borne and has not borne," the Scripture says, as if from itself, not having conceived from a union.

Therefore the Scriptures have been impregnated with the truth for the knowledgeable, but the heresies, not having learned as if they had not been impregnated, are sent away. All people have the same judgment: some follow the choosing word and make their beliefs, while others, having given themselves over to pleasures, force the Scripture toward their desires.

But, I think, the lover of truth needs psychic strength; for it is necessary for those attempting the greatest matters to fail greatly, unless they have taken the standard of truth from truth itself. Such people, having fallen away from the right path, reasonably fail in most things, because they do not have a criterion of true and false things trained precisely to choose what is necessary. For if they had it, they would obey the divine Scriptures.
